key_insight: A two-stage machine-learning workflow—broad pretraining on diverse perovskite structures plus targeted fine-tuning for a passivating molecule—enables atomistic modeling of realistic hybrid halide perovskite surface passivation.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical route to design and optimize molecular defect passivation strategies that can improve perovskite solar-cell stability and optoelectronic performance.
method: Build a large open training set of metal and hybrid halide perovskites (hyP-26).
Fine-tune on a small specialized amino-silane/perovskite surface dataset.
Simulate how passivation behavior changes with molecular surface coverage.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a curated large dataset plus a specialized fine-tuning dataset and uses them to study coverage-dependent interactions at a mixed-composition perovskite surface.
watch_item: The approach may be sensitive to dataset quality and transferability, especially when extrapolating to new surface chemistries or passivating molecules.
paper_title: Data-driven atomistic modelling of hybrid halide perovskite passivation
